text:
Maya: Quick FYI — opened a docs PR to add a compact Terraform + SDK example for Dedicated provisioning that shows autoscale_policy + isolation tags. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/432
Chris: Reviewing now. One thing: the SLA wording in the table currently implies preemption is treated the same as node failure. We should clarify differences.
Maya: Good call. I added a TODO in the PR to reword the SLA row for 'preemption' vs 'eviction' — want a short sentence and a link to the runtime preemption doc.
Jamal: @Maya can you paste the autoscale policy sample you used? want to validate it's operationally safe for burst-to-reserved scenarios.
Maya: Sure — here's the snippet I used in the docs (Terraform):
```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "example" {
  name = "prod-dedicated"
  gpu_type = "a100-80gb"
  reserved_capacity = 40

  autoscale_policy {
    min_replicas = 2
    max_replicas = 20
    cpu_threshold = 0.6
    burst_to_reserved = true
    cooldown_seconds = 120
  }

  isolation_tags = ["team:payments", "slo:low-latency"]
}
```
Sofia: Thanks. Two UX notes for the docs: 1) show a short SDK snippet (python) next to the TF example, 2) call out the tradeoff of burst_to_reserved (cost spike vs. latency safety).
Maya: Will add a compact SDK example under the snippet. Draft python example:
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(pool_name="prod-dedicated")
client.provision(
  autoscale_policy={
    "min":2, "max":20, "burst_to_reserved":True
  },
  isolation_tags=["team:payments"]
)
```
Chris: Small nit: use consistent field names between TF and SDK (`min_replicas` vs `min`). Either normalize or call out mapping in a tiny table.
Maya: I'll normalize to `min_replicas`/`max_replicas` in both.
docs-bot: CI check passed for docs build (link: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/987) :white_check_mark:
Jamal: On isolation: we should add a one-line note about eviction isolation not being a guarantee — it's soft affinity on some clouds. See platform note: https://internal.redwood/inference/isolation-behavior
Maya: Added a short callout and linked that internal note. Also added an examples appendix for migration: how to move from shared -> reserved pools (step-by-step).
Sofia: Great — can you also add a short troubleshooting bullet list: common errors like quota_exceeded, invalid_isolation_tag, and quick remediations? PMs often ask for that.
Maya: Yep, adding a 3-bullet troubleshooting section and a small example of retry/backoff for provisioning in the SDK.
Chris: After those changes I'll approve. Also check wording in the SLA table: replace 'SLA: 99.9%' with 'target: 99.9% (exclusions: planned maintenance, preemption)'.
Maya: Ack. I'll update and push. Thanks all :raised_hands:
Sofia: Marking this as high priority for the next docs release.
Maya: PR updated with fixes + SDK normalization + troubleshooting + SLA rephrase. Thanks for the quick reviews.
Chris: LGTM once CI passes.
Jamal: One follow-up spike item: we should add a short recipe for converting autoscale_policy to a canary rollout config. I'll open a separate PR for that.
Maya: Cool — I'll link it from this PR as a "see also".
Sofia: Thanks everyone.
Maya: Closing thread — merging after CI green.
